title: Mapping the Migraine Cycle Using MRI, CGRP, and Pain Modulation
summary: This study examines how brain activity and certain biological processes change in people with migraines during a migraine attack. To this end, repeated brain scans, pain tests, and tear fluid samples are collected and compared with those of healthy individuals.

interventions.name: Prospective longitudinal observational study of episodic migraine. Over the course of five migraine cycles, repeated MRI scans, tear samples for biomarker analysis, pain tests, and questionnaire surveys are conducted at various stages of the migraine cycle. Healthy control subjects are also examined

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
20 patients with episodic migraine, with and without aura, aged 18 to 60  
Diagnosis is based on the IHS classification (International Headache Society) (Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (IHS), 2018).  
Attack duration of 6 to 10 days (frequency: 3 to 5 per month) 
No prophylactic medications 3 months prior to and during the 
study period 
No acute analgesics taken 24 hours prior to imaging 
No consumption of caffeinated substances 12 hours prior to imaging
Exclusion criteria:
Psychiatric or other neurological conditions other than migraine (see above) 
Chronic pain (e.g., chronic migraine, tension headaches, or chronic back pain) 
Acute pain at the time of the measurement series 
Severe systemic diseases 
Pregnancy/breastfeeding 
MRI-incompatible implants (e.g., pacemakers) 
Claustrophobia
Arterial hypertension or blood pressure > 140/90 mmHg (possible effects of arterial hypertension on CGRP levels)
Eye diseases (e.g., dry eyes)
